device.name: Bluetooth LED Name Badge
device.notes: Monochrome LED dot-matrix name badge. Sold under many brands on AliExpress. Matrix height 11, 12, or 16 rows; width is variable per text/image content. All three heights are fully supported app-side (LedDataUtil.java:577 handles 16 rows; the app bundles 16-row font assets ASC16/HZK16/JPK16/KRK16/TWK16). Protocol is write-only in practice (no useful reads). Data is written in 16-byte chunks: a 64-byte header (4 chunks) followed by stripe-major bitmap data — the message is split into 8-column-wide stripes of `height` bytes each, and each byte is one row of 8 pixels, MSB = leftmost pixel. Writes are ACKNOWLEDGED (writeCharacteristic, NOT write_without_response), with a 3-second per-write ack timeout, 300 ms delay before the first data chunk and 25 ms between subsequent chunks. Up to 8 message slots with per-slot flash and marquee. NO CRC/checksum anywhere in the send path, and NO length prefix at the BLE write level (raw 16-byte chunks). Device stores messages in flash and persists across power cycles. No pairing required. The badge only advertises after the user enters BLE transfer mode (press the lower button twice; a Bluetooth icon shows on the display). Advertised name is filtered by contains("LS") (app-confirmed: BLEScanner.java:154, MainPresenter.java:289). Vendor app ecosystem active: com.yannis.ledcard v3.6.4 (versionCode 64); this spec is verified against a full jadx decompile of v3.6.4. NOTE: AliExpress sellers ship mixed generations under the same listings — a newer badge generation uses a different, AES-encrypted protocol (github.com/timhodson/ble-led-badge), not this "wang"/LSLED one. An open replacement firmware for CH582M-based badges exists (fossasia/badgemagic-firmware). CONFIDENCE: HIGH (full jadx decompile of com.yannis.ledcard v3.6.4; cross-checked against Elektor Jan/Feb 2023 sniff, Nilhcem, FOSSASIA and Doridian). Evidence (v3.6.4 jadx): BleDevice.java:11-20 (name "LS", service 0000fee0, char 0000fee1); LedDataUtil.java:153-177 (get64() header byte-for-byte), 352-355 (per-slot length stored big-endian via byte swap); MainMode.java:59-109 (64-byte header as 4 chunks, bitmap zero-padded into 16-byte chunks); MainPresenter.java:114,122,391 (300 ms before the first data chunk, 25 ms between chunks, 3 s per-write ack timeout); BLEService.java:239-242 (writeCharacteristic with no setWriteType = default acknowledged write). No CRC/checksum code anywhere in the app sources; service 0xFEE7 and characteristics 0xFEC7-FEC9 are never referenced by the app.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the badge advertises only after the user puts it in BLE transfer mode (press the lower button twice until the Bluetooth icon appears on the display) and then accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the badge, then press the lower button twice to enter BLE transfer mode (Bluetooth icon shows).
steps.expect: Badge starts advertising as LSLED (name prefix LS).

steps.action: Scan for its advertisement and connect.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. These badges are widely reported as finicky to connect: they accept one central at a time and often need a power cycle between clients. This is user-reported, device-side behavior; the decompiled v3.6.4 app contains no connection-management code that bears on it, so there is no app-side evidence either way.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

write_badge_data.description: Write badge payload in 16-byte chunks. First 4 chunks are the 64-byte header; subsequent chunks are stripe-major bitmap pixel data (8-column stripes x `height` rows, one row of 8 px per byte, MSB = leftmost pixel). 64-byte header layout (LedDataUtil.get64): Bytes 0-3: Magic "wang" = 0x77 0x61 0x6E 0x67. Byte 4: reserved (0x00). Byte 5: brightness (0x00=100%, 0x10=75%, 0x20=50%, 0x40=25%) -- reads as 0x00 (100%) in the captured get64 trace, per the FOSSASIA badgemagic layout. Byte 6: flash bits (bit N = slot N blinks). Byte 7: marquee bits (bit N = slot N marquee/animated border). Bytes 8-15: mode+speed per slot, one byte each (upper nibble = speed-1, lower nibble = mode-1). Bytes 16-31: message length per slot (uint16 big-endian / MSB-first, 8 slots; Elektor sniff of the vendor app sends 00 07 for length 7). Bytes 32-37: reserved (zeros). Bytes 38-43: date (year, month, day, hour, minute, second). Bytes 44-62: reserved (zeros). Byte 63: 0x00.

characteristics.name: Badge Data
characteristics.notes: GATT properties are read+write+notify (Elektor Table 1, FOSSASIA BadgeBLE.md), but reads/notifications return nothing useful — the protocol is write-only in practice. checksum OMITTED: the device uses NO CRC/checksum (confirmed absent). length_prefix false: raw 16-byte chunks with no BLE-level length prefix.

services.name: Badge Secondary Service
services.notes: Second service present on the badge (Elektor Jan/Feb 2023, Table 1). Undocumented; the vendor app never references it.
